prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: EN · Issue tracker (language en).
Grid: 6 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "ID" · longest unbreakable word 39px · one-line width 75px
  col 2: header "Title" · longest unbreakable word 92px · one-line width 394px
  col 3: header "Severity" · longest unbreakable word 59px · one-line width 59px
  col 4: header "Assignee" · longest unbreakable word 66px · one-line width 66px
  col 5: header "Status" · longest unbreakable word 61px · one-line width 77px
  col 6: header "Updated" · longest unbreakable word 62px · one-line width 87px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
This table cannot fit without splitting words at 360px. You MAY choose a total wider than 359px (the reader then scrolls horizontally), or squeeze and accept splits — a design decision.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

These are all candidate designs you produced, rendered in a real browser:
Design r1B: widths [96, 119, 80, 87, 98, 108] · table 589×673px · row heights [36, 106, 83, 129, 106, 83, 129] · column headers wrapped 0/6 · tallest cell 5 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 229px
Design r1C: widths [96, 160, 80, 87, 98, 108] · table 630×487px · row heights [36, 83, 60, 83, 83, 60, 83] · column headers wrapped 0/6 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 270px
Design r2A: widths [60, 190, 80, 87, 82, 83] · table 583×464px · row heights [36, 83, 60, 83, 60, 60, 83] · column headers wrapped 0/6 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 223px
Design r2B: widths [60, 150, 80, 87, 82, 83] · table 543×511px · row heights [36, 83, 60, 106, 83, 60, 83] · column headers wrapped 0/6 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 183px
Design r2C: widths [60, 220, 80, 87, 82, 83] · table 613×418px · row heights [36, 60, 60, 83, 60, 60, 60] · column headers wrapped 0/6 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 253px
Design r3A: widths [96, 170, 80, 87, 82, 83] · table 599×464px · row heights [36, 83, 60, 83, 60, 60, 83] · column headers wrapped 0/6 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 239px
Design r3B: widths [96, 130, 80, 87, 82, 83] · table 559×627px · row heights [36, 106, 83, 129, 106, 60, 106] · column headers wrapped 0/6 · tallest cell 5 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 199px
Design r3C: widths [96, 150, 80, 87, 98, 108] · table 620×511px · row heights [36, 83, 60, 106, 83, 60, 83] · column headers wrapped 0/6 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 260px

Decide as a designer:
- "preferred": the best design(s). Name more than one only if they are genuinely equally good.
- "acceptable": other designs a careful designer would still publish.
- "bad": designs with clear visual faults, each with the fault. If none of these is clearly bad, also return ONE deliberately bad but plausible alternative as "contrast" widths and say what is wrong with it.
- "ranges": for each column, the px range within which the preferred design stays equally good (keep other columns' proportions).
- "rationale": 2–4 concrete sentences about this table.
- "principles": observations that seem GENERAL (likely to hold for other tables) vs SPECIFIC to this case.
- "tradeoffs" and "uncertain": what reasonable designers could disagree on.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"preferred":["name"],"acceptable":["name"],"bad":[{"design":"name","why":""}],"contrast":{"widths":[int px],"why":""} or null,"ranges":[[min,max]],"rationale":"","principles":{"general":[""],"specific":[""]},"tradeoffs":"","uncertain":""}

log.raw: {"preferred":["r1C"],"acceptable":["r3A","r3C"],"bad":[{"design":"r1B","why":"Title is only 119px, forcing most issue titles into 4–5 lines and stretching rows to 106–129px; the table becomes 673px tall and the title column no longer scans as prose."},{"design":"r2A","why":"ID is only 60px, so every BUG-#### identifier breaks across two lines, undermining the key column just to widen Title."},{"design":"r2B","why":"Combines the ID fault of r2A with a still-too-narrow 150px Title, producing split identifiers and 4-line titles without gaining a coherent layout."},{"design":"r2C","why":"ID is split in every row while Title is over-allocated at 220px; the table still overflows and the most stable identifier is the least intact."},{"design":"r3B","why":"Title at 130px forces 5-line titles and 627px table height; the narrow prose column destroys the table’s vertical rhythm."}],"contrast":null,"ranges":[[96,104],[160,180],[80,88],[87,94],[98,106],[108,116]],"rationale":"r1C is the cleanest compromise: ID stays on one line, and Severity, Assignee, Status and Updated each get exactly enough width for their one-line content, while Title wraps as prose to at most three lines. Its 630px width costs more horizontal scroll than r3A, but it avoids wrapping short metadata such as status and dates. r3A is close but starves Status and Updated below their one-line needs; r2A and r2C buy title width by breaking every BUG-#### identifier. The compressed-title designs (r1B, r2B, r3B) are clearly worse because they turn issue titles into tall stacks of words.","principles":{"general":["Give atomic columns—identifiers, dates, statuses—their one-line widths before allocating leftover space to prose columns.","A primary descriptive column should dominate the grid; equal widths or symmetry are not goals in a table like this.","Breaking an identifier across lines usually costs more scanning clarity than accepting horizontal scroll.","On narrow screens, a table that scrolls horizontally is often better than a false fit that fragments cells."],"specific":["Issue titles are prose and may wrap; BUG-#### identifiers should stay intact.","Severity, Assignee, Status and Updated are short metadata columns with one-line minima around 80, 87, 98 and 108px including padding.","At 360px this six-column issue tracker cannot fit, so the design decision is which columns remain intact.","Status and Updated widths below roughly 98px and 108px are likely to wrap values even when row heights hide it."]},"tradeoffs":"A reasonable designer could prefer r3A or r2C for shorter rows and a wider Title, accepting wrapped metadata or split IDs. r1C deliberately spends about 30px more horizontal width than r3A to keep all non-title cells on one line.","uncertain":"The actual Status and Updated strings are not visible in the overview, so it is uncertain whether r3A’s 82/83px columns merely wrap gracefully or visibly damage scanning; r1C’s 630px total may also feel like too much horizontal scroll on a phone."}
